source.title: Scaling-up Diverse Orthogonal Convolutional Networks by a Paraunitary Framework
source.authors: Jia-Hao Su; Wonmin Byeon; Furong Huang

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendix are present. Figure 7 provides no recoverable numerical training-accuracy values in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training accuracy for WideResNet22-10 across loss margins, but does not report training classification error numerically or test the claim versions' specific conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper's skip-connection comparisons report clean and PGD test accuracy, not training error. Initialization comparisons report clean and PGD test accuracy, not training speed or trainability. Those results are not rows. Figure 7 is the only stated result on training accuracy; the text describes its trend, but the values are figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study uses orthogonal layers to preserve norms and builds Lipschitz networks for robustness. Its skip, depth and initialization comparisons report test accuracy, not training error, training speed or trainable depth. Figure 7 reports a training-accuracy trend across margins but provides no readable outcome establishing near-zero training error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors establish a paraunitary framework for orthogonal convolutions, implement an exact parameterization covering separable orthogonal convolutions, and scale Lipschitz networks to deeper architectures. Their experiments favor additive skips and economical implementations. The stated margin trend is accurate. Initialization conclusions are inconsistent: Section 6.3 favors identical initialization, whereas Appendix D.2 favors permutation; Table 6 gives permutation the highest robust accuracy for WideResNet22-10.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains Lipschitz-constrained orthogonal networks with Adam and multi-class hinge loss to evaluate robustness and architecture choices; it does not use the recipes or primary training-error measures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Training and test accuracy increase with larger hinge-loss margin; robust accuracy decreases after ε0 = 0.1, as described for Figure 7.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 7 states that training and test accuracy increase with larger hinge-loss margins, while robust accuracy decreases beyond a margin of 0.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hinge-loss margin controls the trade-off between classification accuracy and adversarial robustness in the tested orthogonal WideResNet22-10.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 4 reports clean/PGD test accuracy of 69.59/59.22 without skips, 75.21/66.00 with concatenative skips and 87.82/76.46 with additive skips.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additive skips improve clean and robust test accuracy in the tested deep Lipschitz architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 6 compares initialization using final clean and PGD test accuracy, without reporting learning curves or training failure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization affects final predictive performance in orthogonality-constrained WideResNets.

record.problems: Figure 7's training-accuracy values are not recoverable from the supplied text; the paper gives only the trend. The experiment reports best accuracy across five seeds in Section 6.2, rather than uncertainty estimates for the training-accuracy comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Clean and PGD test-accuracy comparisons in Tables 3–6 are not training-error outcomes and do not measure the behaviors named in the versions.

untested.parts: Whether large convolutional networks reach zero or near-zero training classification error; corrupted labels, model-size effects, early stopping and regularized-recipe comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts; very deep plain tanh and Fixup cases.
Initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds, recovery and divergence.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and matched Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Training accuracy is relevant to V1 in principle, but the available qualitative margin trend does not establish its near-zero endpoint or a substantial-error counterexample. Test-accuracy gains and computational efficiency do not establish the optimization outcomes named in V3, V4 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large convolutional networks reach zero or near-zero training error from random initialization, including with corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Whether depth raises training error in plain networks and whether shortcuts prevent that; special initialization and normalization-free residual cases.
Whether initialization changes training speed or trainable depth in plain networks, including the named initialization comparisons.
Training behavior above stability limits, sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Whether batch normalization speeds training or allows higher learning rates, and whether Fixup enables normalization-free residual training.

rows.subject: WideResNet22-10
rows.operation_detail: Trained with different multi-class hinge-loss margins; training accuracy compared across margins.

conditions.value: larger margins; exact plotted values not recoverable from supplied text

rows.note: The text says training accuracy becomes higher with larger margin; it gives no numerical values. This margin comparison is not covered by the listed versions.
rows.check: The larger-margin training-accuracy trend is explicitly stated, but absolute training accuracy cannot be recovered, so it cannot establish V1's near-zero training error. The tested margins are recoverable: 0.001, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2 and 0.5. Keep this as a qualitative margin-comparison finding.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
